_comment:
Per-pin ADC defaults so the temperature_combined sensor in temperature.cfg sees ~25 C across all three legs (PT1000 on PK1, AD595 on PK5, PT100 INA826 on PK6). Otherwise klippy's max_deviation=20.0 deviation check trips because each sensor type's ADC-to-temp curve maps a single global default to a wildly different temperature.

Values:
  PK1 (PT1000):       1097 ohm at 25 C, 4700 pullup -> ratio 0.189 -> ADC = 0.189 * 8184 = 1549
  PK5 (AD595):        0.250 V at 25 C, 5 V ref      -> ratio 0.050 -> ADC = 0.050 * 8184 = 409
  PK6 (PT100 INA826): 1.217 V at 25 C, 5 V ref      -> ratio 0.243 -> ADC = 0.243 * 8184 = 1992
The other ADC pins on this cfg (PF3 custom thermistor, PF4 my_custom_adc, PF5 my_custom_resistance_adc) fall back to the global 5000 default - they aren't part of the combined sensor and only need to stay inside their own min/max, which 5000 satisfies.

spi_response: 17-byte queue aligned to one polling cycle of the four SPI thermocouples (MAX6675 + MAX31855 + MAX31856 LTCBH+SR + MAX31865 RTDMSB+faultstat). The bridge round-robins these bytes through the SPI MISO IRQ; per-cycle alignment lets each thermocouple reader decode a value within its [min_value, max_value] range so klippy doesn't trip 'Thermocouple reader fault'. The 6 leading bytes of the queue happen to also serve as the don't-care MISO data for klippy's two register-write transfers at startup (config writes that the chips' drivers issue before polling begins).

config_overrides raises test_combined's maximum_deviation to 30.0 on the emulator's materialized cfg copy only (the shared temperature.cfg keeps the upstream 20.0): temperature_combined fires its first deviation check 1 s after klippy:ready (see temperature_combined.py _handle_ready), and under the emulator each underlying thermistor's first sample lands 1.5 s into print time (mcu.py get_query_slot), so on a slow firmware bootstrap one leg can still read the 0.0 default while another already shows ~23.9 C. 30.0 bridges that startup window without weakening the steady-state check (settled deviation runs 0-1 C); real hardware boots fast enough that all legs settle inside the upstream default.
